lesson_title: From One Bucket to Five Jobs
hook_text: He started with R200 and a bucket. Now five young people have jobs because of him.
clip_script: No job after matric. Bongani sees dusty taxis every afternoon. R200 buys buckets, sponges and soap. R40 a wash. He writes down every rand. Three months later: a second-hand pressure washer. Business grows, so he hires two friends. A mentor helps him register and get a small grant for a shade and a water-recycling tank. Lower costs, less water wasted. Today, five people earn an income. That is a sustainable job: it lasts, it pays and it does not wreck the environment. Government builds the roads, business invests, communities buy local, and entrepreneurs like Bongani do the rest.
visual_style: A whiteboard taxi rank with a single stick figure and a bucket that grows into a small business with five workers, a recycling tank and a sign.
mood: Inspiring and grounded, a real hustle story.
pacing: Quick montage of growth steps, then a calm list of partners.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and spot one need in your community that could become a small business.
